solution.p: We differentiate implicitly both sides of the equation with respect to x. \ln y + \frac xy \, \frac{dy}{dx} + 3 y^{2}\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6}{x}, so \left( \frac{x}{y} + 3 y^{2} \right) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6}{x} - \ln y, and thus \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\frac{6}{x} - \ln y}{\frac{x}{y} + 3 y^{2}} = \frac{y\mathopen{}\left(6-x\ln\mathopen{}\left(y\right)\right)}{x\mathopen{}\left(x+3y^{3}\right)}.
